verses.zh: 「人若娶妻以后，见她有甚么不合理的事，不喜悦她，就可以写休书交在她手中，打发她离开夫家。
verses.en: If a man marries a woman and she does not please him because he has found something indecent[NOTE:1] in her, then he may draw up a divorce document, give it to her, and evict her from his house.
notes: The Hebrew phrase עֶרְוַת דָּבָר (ʿervat davar) involves a genitive of specification, something characterized by עֶרְוָה (ʿervah). עֶרְוָה means “nakedness,” and by extension means “shame, sexual impropriety, sexual organs, indecency” (NIDOTTE III 528, Jastrow 1114-15).
verses.commentary:
24:1-4 "When. . .if. . .then" This construction is a Qal PERFECT with waw
(BDB 224, KB 243) of "come to pass" with the hypothetical PARTICLE (BDB 49). This hypothetical situation is
continued for the first three verses. Verses 1-4 are one sentence with the conclusion stated in Deut. 24:4. Notice that this is
not a general discussion on divorce, but a special case of divorce, remarriage, and divorce/death and remarriage to the original
partner. It is difficult to draw too many universal truths from this context. Even Jesus discussion about this passage and
the issue of divorce is colored by the religious leaders' attempts to trap Him in controversy for the purpose of reducing His
support among the people and to find legal/theological grounds to charge Him. Divorce has never been the best option!

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVORCE

▣ "she finds no favor in his eyes" This common VERB (BDB 592, KB 619) is used twice in
this verse (first, Qal IMPERFECT and the second Qal PERFECT). It is used in the
sense of "to recognize an existing condition" (cf. Deut. 22:14,17).

The term "favor" (BDB 336) is used of both God's favor (e.g. Gen. 6:8; Exod. 33:17) and mankind's
(e.g. Gen. 30:27; 33:8,10,15; Ruth 2:2,10,13). It means a favorable acceptance or attitude of responsiveness. Here it is
negated. It recognized the fallen condition of human love, which is sometimes fickle, fleeting, and selfish.

This text has been a source of great controversy among the rabbis. Shammai (the conservative
group of rabbis) said it only referred to adultery, while Hillel (the liberal group of rabbis) said it could refer to anything,
even trivial things (i.e. bad food, bad in-law relations, found a prettier woman). In Israel only the husband had the legal
right of divorce (unless Exod. 21:11 is an example; a later example is the "Elephantine Papyri" of the fifth century B.C.).

▣

NASB
"some indecency"

NKJV
"some uncleanness"

NRSV
"something objectionable"

TEV
"something about her that he doesn't like"

NJB
"some impropriety"

JPSOA
"something obnoxious"

REB
"something offensive"

LXX
"a shameful thing"

Peshitta
"some evidence of open prostitution"

Literally this is "the nakedness of a thing" (BDB 788). In Deut. 23:14 the same term is used in a
non-moral sense. This cannot refer to proven adultery because the automatic penalty was death (cf. Deut. 22:22). Jesus,
when quoting this text, seems to interpret it by the phrase "fornication" in Matt. 19:9, which was a Greek term
(porneia) that involved any sexual impropriety or unfaithfulness. The term is meant to be ambiguous and, thereby
covers the widest possible circumstances.

Moses wrote this text to protect the rejected, vulnerable wife. It is shocking to me that Jesus asserts
that this legal protection of divorce and remarriage was never God's intention (cf. Matt. 5:27-32; 19:7-12; Mark 10:2-12;
Luke 16:14-18), but Moses' idea because of the hardness of the hearts of the Israelites. How many other things recorded
in the Pentateuch are not the intended will of God? Jesus, as Lord of Scripture, showed His authority by correcting both
OT texts and their interpretation (cf. Matt. 5:17-48; Mark 7:1-23). This is distressing to us modern evangelicals who put
such an emphasis on the Bible as the "word of God" (and it surely is!), but we must remember that Jesus is the Living
Word and we only have a fraction of all the things He did and said (cf. John 20:30). The Bible is primarily designed to
first give us salvation (cf. John 20:31; 2 Tim. 3:15) and then to guide us in living the Christian life (cf. 2 Tim.3:16-17). We
have all the information that we need to be saved and live a life pleasing to God. We do not need additional rules and
laws. The texts we have and the indwelling Spirit guide us from the texts we have into the areas of uncertainty. I am
reminded that Jesus commented that all Scriptural teaching on how to live for God is summed up in only two priority
statements (cf. Matt. 22:34-40; Mark 12:28-34; Luke 10:25-28):

- Deut. 6:4-5 ‒ love God completely

- Lev. 19:18 ‒ love your neighbor as yourself

SPECIAL TOPIC: CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE

▣ "certificate of divorce" This was a legal document of separation. It may have involved giving
back the dowry. This later required an involved legal procedure which hopefully gave time for the partners to reconcile,
but here it seems to be written by the husband or his representative (i.e. a Levite).

Divorce and remarriage are also discussed in relation to priests in Lev. 21:7,14 and 22:13. It must have
been common (cf. Num. 30:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE

verses.zh: 妇人离开夫家以后，可以去嫁别人。
verses.en: When she has left him[NOTE:1] she may go and become someone else’s wife.
notes: Heb “his house.”
verses.commentary:
24:2 "becomes another man's wife" The right of remarriage was assumed and stated. This was the very
purpose of the procedure.

verses.zh: 后夫若恨恶她，写休书交在她手中，打发她离开夫家，或是娶她为妻的后夫死了，
verses.en: If the second husband rejects[NOTE:1] her and then divorces her,[NOTE:2] gives her the papers, and evicts her from his house, or if the second husband who married her dies,
notes: Heb “hates.” See note on the word “other” in Deut 21:15.
Heb “writes her a document of divorce.”
verses.commentary:
24:3 "if the latter husband turns against her" The word "if" is not in the Hebrew MSS. It is assuming another
hypothetical situation (like Deut. 24:1).

The VERB "turns against" is literally "hates" (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal
PERFECT with waw) and was used in Aramaic for "divorce."

▣ "if the latter husband dies" This is another possible scenario.

verses.zh: 打发她去的前夫不可在妇人玷污之后再娶她为妻，因为这是耶和华所憎恶的；不可使耶和华―你　神所赐为业之地被玷污了。」
verses.en: her first husband who divorced her is not permitted to remarry[NOTE:1] her after she has become ritually impure, for that is offensive to the Lord.[NOTE:2] You must not bring guilt on the land[NOTE:3] that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
notes: Heb “to return to take her to be his wife.”
The issue here is not divorce and its grounds per se but prohibition of remarriage to a mate whom one has previously divorced.
Heb “cause the land to sin” (so KJV, ASV).
verses.commentary:
24:4 "her former husband. . .is not allowed to take her again to be his wife" The original couple are encouraged
to reconcile (legal procedures of the bill of divorcement), but once separated and the wife remarries, reconciliation is
forbidden! This is the purpose of all of the conditions found in Deut. 24:1-3. This may have been a way to protect the
second marriage.

▣ "she has been defiled" The defilement (BDB 379 I, KB 375, Hothpaal PERFECT),
was related to knowing two different men sexually, which would make the original husband taking her again a type of
adultery! This "defilement" related only to the first husband, not the woman.

The ambiguity of the wording of the paragraph makes it difficult to pronounce universal spiritual
principles. This is not a context on the evil of divorce and remarriage, but on the first husband taking his divorced
wife again after a second marriage. Divorce and remarriage were common and not condemned in the ANE.

The IVP Bible Background Commentary has an interesting comment:

"The very unusual form of the Hebrew verb used in verse 4 makes it clear that the woman in
this case is the victim, not the guilty party. She has been forced to declare her uncleanness by the uncharitable
actions of the first husband, and the second marriage demonstrates that another husband has been capable
of accommodating whatever 'impurity' she was plagued with. The prohibition is aimed at preventing the first
husband from marrying the woman again (in which case he might be able to realize some financial gain), whereas
if the woman were impure the prohibition would be against her and would preclude a marriage relationship with
anyone" (p. 198).

▣ "an abomination" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

▣ "you shall not bring sin on the land" YHWH desires strong, godly marriages and families. They provide
strength, stability, and education for the next generation of covenant people. Marriage is modeled more than taught! Divorce
is not the sin, but the first husband taking back his wife after another husband!

Two Prophets use this passage as imagery to describe God's dealing with Israel's faithlessness
(Isa. 50:1; Jer. 3:1,8). Going after other gods was considered "spiritual adultery."

verses.zh: 「新娶妻之人不可从军出征，也不可托他办理甚么公事，可以在家清闲一年，使他所娶的妻快活。
verses.en: When a man is newly married, he need not go into[NOTE:1] the army nor be obligated in any way; he must be free to stay at home for a full year and bring joy to[NOTE:2] the wife he has married.
notes: Heb “go out with.”
For the MT’s reading Piel שִׂמַּח (simmakh, “bring joy to”), the Syriac and others read שָׂמַח (samakh, “enjoy”).
verses.commentary:
24:5 "When a man takes a new wife" The new husband was not required to serve in the army or perform
other civic duties for one year. This was for the purpose of insuring an heir (cf. Deut. 20:7).

▣ "shall give happiness to his wife" This VERB (BDB 970, KB 1333, Piel PERFECT
with waw) means "to rejoice" or "be glad." This was YHWH's purpose for His covenant people. The laws of Deuteronomy
were to aid fallen humanity to obtain and maintain a happy, content society.

The NIDOTTE, vol. 3, p. 1252, has a good quote on this subject:

"Joy should also be prominent in family relationships. Moses exhorts the new husband to
devote himself to make his wife happy (Deut. 24:5) and the sage counsels the husband to rejoice in the wife
of his youth (Prov. 5:18).

verses.zh: 「不可拿人的全盘磨石或是上磨石作当头，因为这是拿人的命作当头。
verses.en: One must not take either lower or upper millstones as security on a loan, for that is like taking a life itself as security.[NOTE:1]
notes: Taking millstones as security on a loan would amount to taking the owner’s own life in pledge, since the millstones were the owner’s means of earning a living and supporting his family.
verses.commentary:
24:6 "handmill or an upper millstone" This refers to the upper stone of a two-stone grinding mill
(BDB 932, 939, cf. Exod. 11:5; Jdgs. 9:53; 2 Sam. 11:21), which was used to prepare daily bread. The upper part
was useless without the matching bottom piece.

▣ "in pledge" This term, "in pledge," (BDB 286, KB 285) basically means "to bind." When one
borrows he is obligated to repay. To secure this repayment (without interest to a fellow Israelite) the creditor
could take something of value and hold it:

- grinding stone, Deut. 24:6

- garments, Deut. 24:17; Exod. 22:25-27; Job 24:7,10

- ancestral land and houses, Neh. 5:3 (possibly Job 24:2)

- an essential animal, Job 24:3

- essential help, the children, Exod. 21:7; Lev. 25:39-43; 2 Kgs. 4:1; Job 24:9

Each of these items were a necessary part of daily agricultural existence. To remove any one of these
jeopardized the family, even life itself. YHWH's compassion and care for Israel was to be emulated by those Israelites
who had resources. YHWH would bless them for their compassion. They would be given more so that they could share
more (cf. Deut. 24:13; 2 Cor. 9:6-10).

verses.zh: 「若遇见人拐带以色列中的一个弟兄，当奴才待他，或是卖了他，那拐带人的就必治死。这样，便将那恶从你们中间除掉。
verses.en: If a man is found kidnapping a person from among his fellow Israelites,[NOTE:1] and regards him as mere property[NOTE:2] and sells him, that kidnapper[NOTE:3] must die. In this way you will purge[NOTE:4] the evil from among you.
notes: Heb “from his brothers, from the sons of Israel.” The terms “brothers” and “sons of Israel” are in apposition; the second defines the first more specifically.
Or “and enslaves him.”
Heb “that thief.”
Heb “burn.” See note on the word “purge” in Deut 19:19.
verses.commentary:
24:7 "kidnapping" The Hebrew VERB here is "stealing" (BDB 170, KB 198, Qal
PARTICIPLE). "Kidnaping" was seen as stealing a life (literally, "stealing nephesh, BDB 659; see LXX).
Many believe this is what the Ten Commandments refer to in the command "Thou shall not steal." The penalty for this was
death, which seems severe for simple theft (cf. Exod. 21:16; Deut. 5:19).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STEAL

▣

NASB
"deals. . .violently"

NKJV
"mistreats"

NRSV
"enslaving"

TEV
"make them your slaves"

NJB
"he makes him his slave"

REB
"treated him harshly"

LXX
"overpowered him"

Peshitta
"to make merchandise of him"

The root (BDB 771) has several meanings:

- sheaf, Deut. 24:19 or bind sheaves, Ps. 129:7

- omer ‒ BDB I, Exod. 16:18,22,32,33

- deal tyrannically ‒ BDB II, Deut. 21:14; 24:7

- live long (Arabic root) ‒ BDB III

The pronunciation and context designated which meaning was intended for this trilateral root. Option
#3 is found only twice in the OT, both in Deuteronomy.

▣ "that thief shall die" See SPECIAL TOPIC: DEATH PENALTY IN ISRAEL

▣ "so you shall purge the evil from among you" This is a recurrent idiom. See note at Deut. 13:5
(cf. Deut. 17:7,12; 19:13,19; 21:9,21; 22:21,22,24; Jdgs. 20:13). YHWH dwelt among His people, therefore, His people must be holy (i.e. Lev. 19:2).

verses.zh: 「在大麻疯的灾病上，你们要谨慎，照祭司利未人一切所指教你们的留意遵行。我怎样吩咐他们，你们要怎样遵行。
verses.en: Be careful during an outbreak of leprosy to follow precisely[NOTE:1] all that the Levitical priests instruct you; as I have commanded them, so you should do.
notes: Heb “to watch carefully and to do.”
verses.commentary:
24:8 "Be careful" The VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581) is used three times in this verse:

- Niphal IMPERATIVE, "be careful"

- Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, plus the ADVERB "very" (BDB 547)
and the VERB "to do" (BDB 793, KB 889, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)

- Qal IMPERFECT, "careful to do" plus VERB "to do" (BDB 793,
KB 889, Qal IMPERFECT)

The basic meaning is "to keep," "to watch," or "to preserve." Careful obedience to YHWH's guidelines
is stressed by the three-fold repetition.

▣ "leprosy" This (BDB 863) is not the modern disease as we know it (i.e. Hansen's disease). This term covered many different
things (i.e. skin, clothes, leather, houses). The guidelines and procedures are discussed in Leviticus 13-14. This implies
that Leviticus was already available at this time. The Pentateuch is a unified whole. See my notes in Leviticus 13-14 online.

verses.zh: 当记念出埃及后，在路上，耶和华―你　神向米利暗所行的事。
verses.en: Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam[NOTE:1] along the way after you left Egypt.
notes: What the Lord your God did to Miriam. The reference is to Miriam’s having contracted leprosy because of her intemperate challenge to Moses’ leadership (Num 12:1-15). The purpose for the allusion here appears to be the assertion of the theocratic leadership of the priests who, like Moses, should not be despised.
verses.commentary:
24:9 The incident referred to is recorded in Numbers 12, where both Aaron and Miriam complained about
Moses' leadership and marriage to a Cushite woman (black woman). In response YHWH affirms Moses' leadership and
inflicts Miriam with leprosy (Miriam loses her skin pigment), but at Moses' intercession, He restores her darker skin color.

verses.zh: 「你借给邻舍，不拘是甚么，不可进他家拿他的当头。
verses.en: When you make any kind of loan to your neighbor, you may not go into his house to claim what he is offering as security.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his pledge.” This refers to something offered as pledge of repayment, i.e., as security for the debt.
verses.commentary:
24:10 "you shall not enter his house to take his pledge" The honor and privacy of one's home was protected. The borrower
could also choose which garment or household item to use as the pledge.

The VERB (BDB 716, KB 778, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is
intensified by the use of the same NOUN (BDB 716) "pledge." A pledge was a physical object, in this
context, a man's outer garment used as security for a loan (cf. Deut. 24:11-13).

These garments were not very valuable, but were necessary to the daily needs of the poor. Taking a
man's garment was more than security for a loan. It was an expression of contempt for the poor man. In God's eyes all
humans are valuable because they are made in His image and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27). God's covenant people must
recognize the value and worth He places on humans and respond appropriately!

verses.zh: 要站在外面，等那向你借贷的人把当头拿出来交给你。
verses.en: You must stand outside and the person to whom you are making the loan will bring out to you what he is offering as security.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his pledge.”

verses.zh: 他若是穷人，你不可留他的当头过夜。
verses.en: If the person is poor you may not use what he gives you as security for a covering.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “may not lie down in his pledge.” What is in view is the use of clothing as guarantee for the repayment of loans, a matter already addressed elsewhere (Deut 23:19-20; 24:6; cf. Exod 22:25-26; Lev 25:35-37). Cf. NAB “you shall not sleep in the mantle he gives as a pledge”; NRSV “in the garment given you as the pledge.”
verses.commentary:
24:12 "If he is a poor man, you shall not sleep with his pledge" This referred to the outer cloak which the poor
used as a sleep covering (cf. Exod. 22:26-27).

verses.zh: 日落的时候，总要把当头还他，使他用那件衣服盖着睡觉，他就为你祝福；这在耶和华―你　神面前就是你的义了。
verses.en: You must by all means[NOTE:1] return to him at sunset the item he gave you as security so that he may sleep in his outer garment and bless you for it; it will be considered a just deed[NOTE:2] by the Lord your God.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the infinitive absolute for emphasis, which the translation seeks to reflect with “by all means.”
Or “righteous” (so NIV, NLT).
verses.commentary:
24:13 "you shall surely return" This is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE combined with the IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root (BDB 996, KB 1427), which denotes intensity.

▣ "and bless you" YHWH defends the poor, widow, alien, and orphan's rights and person. To abuse
them caused a reaction from YHWH Himself (e.g. Exod. 22:23; Deut. 15:9; 24:15)!

▣ "it will be righteousness for you" The Septuagint understands this term as it is used here to refer to
Jewish "almsgiving" (cf. Deut. 6:25; 15:7-11; Matt. 6:1-4).

verses.zh: 「困苦穷乏的雇工，无论是你的弟兄或是在你城里寄居的，你不可欺负他。
verses.en: You must not oppress a lowly and poor servant, whether one from among your fellow Israelites[NOTE:1] or from the resident foreigners who are living in your land and villages.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your brothers,” but not limited only to actual siblings; cf. NASB, NAB “countrymen.”
Heb “who are in your land in your gates.” The word “living” is supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
24:14 "or one of your aliens" YHWH's care for the widow, orphan, and alien is clearly seen in Deuteronomy
(cf. Deut. 10:18; 14:29; 16:11,14; 24:17,19,20,21; 26:12,13; 27:19). This emphasis was different from other ANE law codes.

verses.zh: 要当日给他工价，不可等到日落―因为他穷苦，把心放在工价上―恐怕他因你求告耶和华，罪便归你了。
verses.en: You must pay his wage that very day before the sun sets, for he is poor and his life depends on it. Otherwise he will cry out to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
verses.commentary:
24:15 "You shall give him his wages on his day" The poor needed (i.e. "set his heart on it") the daily wage to buy
food for himself and his family. The landowner wanted to keep it to assure that the worker would return to work the next
day (cf. Lev. 19:13; Mal. 3:5; James 5:4).

▣ "so that he will not cry against you to the Lord" God cares and hears the cry
of the poor, alienated and ostracized! See note at Deut. 24:13.

▣ "it become sin in you" In context this is the opposite condition of "righteousness" in Deut. 24:13.

verses.zh: 「不可因子杀父，也不可因父杀子；凡被杀的都为本身的罪。
verses.en: Fathers must not be put to death for what their children[NOTE:1] do, nor children for what their fathers do; each must be put to death for his own sin.
notes: Heb “sons” (so NASB; twice in this verse). Many English versions, including the KJV, read “children” here.
verses.commentary:
24:16 This verse is very similar to Ezek. 18:1-33; 17:12-20; Jer. 31:29-30; and 2 Kgs. 14:6. It focuses on the rare
OT concept of individual responsibility. This is a balance to Exod. 20:5; 34:7; Num. 14:18. The OT usually focuses
on corporality (cf. Deut. 5:9).

Notice the three-fold use of the VERB "put to death" (BDB 559, KB 562, all Hophal
IMPERFECTS). Rebellion is a serious matter! Disobedience has consequences!

This law does not refer to rebellion against God (e.g. idolatry), but to actions designated civil
(e.g. acts against established civil authority or acts against a covenant partner).

Humans are held responsible for personal sins, but often these sins are related to family or cultural
practices. All of us are historically, culturally conditioned. We make choices, but these choices are limited by precedent.
Society, family, and individuals are inseparably bound together! All are affected by parents, culture, and personal choices!
God judges society, families, and individuals. Human freedom is a wonderful/terrible gift!

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLICAL FAITH IS CORPORATE

verses.zh: 「你不可向寄居的和孤儿屈枉正直，也不可拿寡妇的衣裳作当头。
verses.en: You must not pervert justice[NOTE:1] due a resident foreigner or an orphan, or take a widow’s garment as security for a loan.
notes: Besides not oppressing the resident foreigner (גֵּר; ger) (Exod 22:21; Deut 24:14, 17; 27:19), Israel was told to love them (Lev 19:33-34; Deut 10:18-19).
verses.commentary:
24:17 "You shall not pervert the justice due" The VERB (BDB 639, KB 692, Hiphil
IMPERFECT) basically means "stretch out," "spread out" or "turn." Often this is used as imagery for
"turn to the right or left and leaving God's clearly revealed law" (cf. Deut. 5:32; 17:11,20; 28:14; Josh. 1:7; 23:6).

There are several places where the object of this turning/perverting is "justice" (BDB 1048, cf. Exod. 23:6;
Deut. 16:19; 24:17; 27:19; 1 Sam. 8:3; Prov. 17:23; Lam. 3:35; and Amos 2:7). Justice is YHWH's will for everyone in Israelite
society because it reflects His character and treatment of them (cf. Deut. 32:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

▣ "alien or an orphan, nor take a widow's garment in pledge" See Deut. 10:18 and Exod. 22:22-24. Moses'
Law Code is different from the other ancient Mesopotamian Law Codes in its care for the poor, needy, and socially powerless!

verses.zh: 要记念你在埃及作过奴仆。耶和华―你的　神从那里将你救赎，所以我吩咐你这样行。
verses.en: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there; therefore I am commanding you to do all this.
verses.commentary:
24:18 "But you shall remember" Notice that this emphasis on remembering (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal PERFECT
with waw) is mentioned three times in this chapter (Deut. 24:9,18,22). The past does affect the future. Israel was to remember
and then act appropriately today (i.e. Deut. 8:11-20)!

▣ "redeemed" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM.

verses.zh: 「你在田间收割庄稼，若忘下一捆，不可回去再取，要留给寄居的与孤儿寡妇。这样，耶和华―你　神必在你手里所办的一切事上赐福与你。
verses.en: Whenever you reap your harvest in your field and leave some unraked grain there,[NOTE:1] you must not return to get it; it should go to the resident foreigner, orphan, and widow so that the Lord your God may bless all the work you do.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the field.”
Heb “of your hands.” This law was later applied in the story of Ruth who, as a poor widow, was allowed by generous Boaz to glean in his fields (Ruth 2:1-13).
verses.commentary:
24:19-21 These agricultural regulations were meant to provide food for the poor and needy (see Lev. 19:9-10;
23:22; Ruth 2). This is called "gleaning."

There are several laws in Deuteronomy about providing food for the needy:

- the third-year local tithe for the poor, Deut. 14:28-29; 26:12-15

- food provided at the celebration of the Feast of Weeks/Feast of Booths, Deut. 16:9-17

- the yearly gleanings from the annual grain harvests, Deut. 24:19-21

verses.zh: 你也要记念你在埃及地作过奴仆，所以我吩咐你这样行。
verses.en: Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt; therefore, I am commanding you to do all this.
verses.commentary:
24:22 The Israelites were to have compassion on servants and aliens because they once shared this condition in
Egypt. YHWH was gracious to them; they, too, should be gracious to others!

Several times in Deuteronomy the call to remember Israel's period of enslavement is used to stimulate current action:

- all in the community to observe the Sabbath, Deut. 5:12-15 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SABBATH)

- release the Israelite slave on the seventh year, Deut. 15:12-18

- all in the community to participate in the Feast of Weeks, Deut. 16:9-17 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL)

- do not pervert justice due an alien or an orphan, nor take a widow's garment in pledge, Deut. 24:17-18

- do not reap all the way to the corners of the field and do not do a second reaping, Deut. 24:19-22 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: GLEANING)

- using other words, but with the same emphasis, obedience, Deut. 6:10-15; 8:2,18 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP)
